sim_assumptions.what: Published bars and box medians read off Figs 2 and 3 (the 2400 x 1200 images in the paper's PDF) through each panel's tick marks
sim_assumptions.sensitivity: Tick fits within 0.22 px; one power point is 3.82 px and every bar reads within 0.2 points of an integer count; Fig. 3 medians within 0.1 of a half-integer. The reading error is far below the Monte Carlo tolerance.

sim_assumptions.what: Disease models: Marchini et al.'s tables of odds for models 1 and 3; for model 2 the table of epiMODE (Tang et al. 2009, the same group), (1+t)^2, (1+t)^3, (1+t)^4 for two, three and four disease alleles, where Marchini has 1+t, (1+t)^2, (1+t)^4
sim_assumptions.sensitivity: Chosen among six documented readings by the exact chi-squared power, which involves no random forest (output/checks/model_variants.json): epiMODE's table puts 21 of the 24 chi-squared bars within Monte Carlo error (8 of 8 in model 2); Marchini's table 17 (4 of 8); either table read as relative risks 18, and Marchini's model 2 at MAF 0.05 to 0.2 cannot reach lambda = 0.5 as relative risks.

sim_assumptions.what: The marginal effect lambda is the odds ratio of the marginal penetrances of the heterozygote and the wild-type homozygote, minus 1 (Zhang and Liu 2007; epiMODE Text S1); prevalence 0.1 for every model (the paper)
sim_assumptions.sensitivity: Prevalence 0.01 for model 2 (epiMODE's setting) puts 15 or 18 of the 24 chi-squared bars within Monte Carlo error instead of 21 (model_variants.json).

sim_assumptions.what: LD between a disease locus and its marker: the marker has the locus's minor allele frequency and each marker allele follows the locus allele on its haplotype with correlation r = sqrt(r2) (epiMODE Text S1); null markers have MAF from U(0, 0.5) (the paper); the two disease markers sit at random columns
sim_assumptions.sensitivity: Using 0.7 as r instead of r2 lowers model 3 at MAF 0.5 to 9% chi-squared power against the published 38% (model_variants.json, epimode_odds_r2_as_r: 19 of 24 bars within Monte Carlo error).

sim_assumptions.what: A disease marker counts as identified when it is in any reported test; power is the share of 100 data sets where both are
sim_assumptions.sensitivity: summary.json gives epiForest's power when both markers must be in one reported test (epiforest_joint) or reported singly (epiforest_one_way).

ef_assumptions.what: ntree = 500 (randomForest's default) for the first forest and every SWSFS forest; the paper gives ntree only for the AMD forests (10^6)
ef_assumptions.sensitivity: With 2000 trees SWSFS keeps still fewer SNPs on the data sets we tried (output/checks/swsfs_variants.json).

ef_assumptions.what: mtry = floor(sqrt(number of SNPs in the forest)), randomForest's default (the paper prints the default garbled)
ef_assumptions.sensitivity: With mtry fixed at 31 for every SWSFS forest: output/checks/swsfs_variants.json.

ef_assumptions.what: B statistic with pseudo-counts 0.5 and P0 in the denominator (the paper prints P1/P1); 2B minus a shift from Stirling's expansion is chi-squared with 3^k - 1 degrees of freedom (3^k - 3^t conditional); the conditional B tests the other markers with the reported ones keeping their association
ef_assumptions.sensitivity: On null data the shifted statistic has the right mean and tail for one- and two-way tests and is conservative for three-way tests (check.bstat_null).

ef_assumptions.what: Bonferroni over all L = 1000 markers (L, L(L-1)/2, L(L-1)(L-2)/6), as the paper says
ef_assumptions.sensitivity: summary.json, epiforest_bonf_candidates: Bonferroni over the candidates instead.

lr_assumptions.what: Stepwise logistic regression: 100 SNPs (10%) kept by their single-locus likelihood-ratio test (2 df, adjusted by L); stage 2 tests every pair and triple of kept SNPs for interaction, the logistic model with one parameter per observed genotype combination against the model with main effects only (4 df for a pair, 20 for a triple), adjusted by L(L-1)/2 and L(L-1)(L-2)/6 as the paper adjusts epiForest's tests; a disease marker is found in any significant test. The paper names the method (Marchini et al. 2005, extended to three-way) but not which models stage 2 compares or how it is adjusted
lr_assumptions.sensitivity: Chosen among five readings by the number of published bars within Monte Carlo error (comparison.json, sensitivity.fig2): this one 17 of 24; interaction terms adjusted by the number of stage-2 tests 14; the full model against the null model (Marchini's two-stage strategy) 4 adjusted by the stage-2 tests and 8 by all tests; single-locus tests alone 19. The full-model readings find a disease marker through its main effect in stage 2, which the single-locus test missed, and run 20 to 70 points above the paper.

render_assumptions.what: Drawn with base R at 12 x 6 in, 200 px per inch (the published 2400 x 1200 px), margins from the published frames; font Liberation Sans (Helvetica metrics); text sizes and offsets matched to the published glyphs. Only ink inside the frames is scored, so the text settings do not change the score

amd_cause.summary: The AMD genotypes (Klein et al. 2005, Affymetrix 100K, 96 cases and 50 controls) came from J. Hoh and were never deposited; the AREDS scan in dbGaP (phs000001) has controlled access, and whether it holds the same 146 people is unverified.

page.lede: {items} results: {exact} exact, {agrees} agree, {partly} partly agree, {differs} differ, {not_attempted} not attempted; {reviewed} verdicts set by a reviewer. epiForest was lost; it was rebuilt from the paper as an R package, and the paper's simulation study of 2,400 data sets was run again.
page.items_caption: Every figure, table and claim of the paper. A power or a median agrees when it is within the Monte Carlo error of two independent sets of 100 data sets (1.96 standard errors of the difference).
page.claims_line: The main claim holds in part: epiForest is never below chi-squared and beats it where interactions matter, but in our run it falls below logistic regression in 4 of 24 settings at small MAF, where the paper has it level or ahead. The causes, in how the paper ran its forests, simulated model 3 and set up logistic regression, are open with the tested candidates recorded; the AMD study needs genotypes that were never released.
came_back: The gini ranking, SWSFS and the hierarchical B-statistic tests, as the R package epiforest, with tests and a tutorial.
20 of 24 bars of Fig. 2 within Monte Carlo error; the four misses are model 3 at small MAF.
17 of 24 bars, with the stage-2 test chosen by its match to these bars (4 of 24 with Marchini et al.'s strategy as published).
Its shift, which the paper does not write out, derived and checked on null data.
buried: The AMD study (Figs 4 to 6, Table 1): the genotypes were never deposited.
BEAM, the fourth method of Fig. 2: its program is gone.
Fig. 3: SWSFS keeps about 32 SNPs where the paper's figure shows 45 to 48 (median 46) in every setting; five readings of the stopping rule and the forests were tested.
How the paper set up its forests, its model 3 and its stage-2 logistic regression: not stated, and no tested reading closes every gap.
page.matched_intro: How each part of the paper's method was rebuilt.
matched: R randomForest 4.7-1.1, SNPs as three-level factors, 500 trees, mtry the square root of the number of SNPs; gini importance.
The paper's pseudocode, window 20, the out-of-bag error of each forest.
One-, two- and three-way, conditional on SNPs already reported; Bonferroni over all tests of each order.
Marchini et al.'s three disease models (model 2 as in epiMODE), 1000 markers, 1000 cases and 1000 controls, 100 data sets per setting.
The single-locus chi-squared test and stepwise logistic regression with three-way interactions.
page.closing: epiForest came back from the paper's text, and its simulation study was run again in full.

fig2.chisq.summary: 20 of 24 bars within Monte Carlo error; all four misses are model 3 at small MAF, where our chi-squared power is higher than the paper's (r2 = 0.7: 26, 72, 99 against 0, 11, 79 at MAF 0.05, 0.1, 0.2; r2 = 1: 64 against 48 at MAF 0.05). The exact power of our model (no simulation) gives the same values, so the gap is in how the paper simulated model 3 or the LD, which it does not state; the documented table, scale and prevalence readings leave model 3's marginal power unchanged, and reading 0.7 as r overshoots in the other direction.

fig2.epiforest.summary: 15 of 24 bars within Monte Carlo error. Where the signal is weak (r2 = 0.7, models 2 and 3, MAF 0.05 to 0.2) ours is higher, as our chi-squared is in model 3; where the paper's epiForest is far ahead of chi-squared (models 2 and 3, r2 = 1, MAF 0.05 and 0.1) ours is lower: 2 against 16, 38 against 57, 87 against 97, 72 against 89. There our first forest ranks a disease marker low (model 2, MAF 0.05: the lower one at rank 800 in median), so neither SWSFS nor the B tests see it. The paper's forest settings are not given; mtry = 100 ranks the markers higher at MAF 0.1 but not at MAF 0.05.
